name: The patent clerk's miracle year
scope: 1905: four papers in six months from a man with no laboratory, no professorship and no PhD yet. T1: the hook is the DAY JOB -- in 1905 an unknown 26-year-old sent Annalen der Physik four papers in six months, any one of which would have made a career; his job was examining electrical patent applications at the Swiss Patent Office in Bern, where his title was 'technical expert, third class' (he had held the post since June 1902 and kept it until 1909). T2: the 1921 Nobel citation names NOT relativity but the March paper on light quanta and the photoelectric effect -- Einstein never won a Nobel for relativity at all. T3: the May paper on Brownian motion settled a live argument -- Ernst Mach and Wilhelm Ostwald still denied atoms were real; Einstein predicted the exact statistical jiggle a pollen grain should perform, and Jean Perrin's 1908-09 measurements matched it (Perrin's 1926 Nobel was for that work). T4: the June relativity paper, 'On the Electrodynamics of Moving Bodies', carried no citations and no bibliography at all; its only acknowledgement is its last line, thanking Michele Besso -- a fellow engineer at the patent office -- for 'several valuable suggestions'. T5: the fourth paper was THREE PAGES long, titled as a question ('Does the inertia of a body depend upon its energy content?'), wrote the result not as E=mc2 but as m = L/V2, and ended by proposing a way to TEST it -- Einstein suggested measuring bodies whose energy content varies enormously, 'e.g. salts of radium'. T5b: in a May 1905 letter to his friend Conrad Habicht, Einstein promised four papers and called only ONE of them 'very revolutionary' -- the light-quantum paper, not relativity. T5c: the papers were written in evenings and weekends, argued out with the 'Olympia Academy' -- Einstein, Habicht and Maurice Solovine reading philosophy and physics together in Bern; Annalen der Physik had no formal peer review, so Max Planck as editor simply decided to print them.
source: Grokipedia 'Annus mirabilis papers' (patent office rank 'technical expert/technical assistant, third class'; submission and publication dates; page counts; no formal peer review; Olympia Academy; Besso and Habicht); Wikipedia 'Annus mirabilis papers' (German titles, received/published dates, 1921 Nobel citation naming the photoelectric effect, L and V notation); Grokipedia 'Mass-energy equivalence' (Einstein's own m = L/V2 derivation, September 1905, Annalen der Physik).
framing_note: DISCOVERY mode; the flagship opener for the whole sub-strand. Voice: scene-led -- a desk, a stack of patent applications, evenings. T1 keys the day job, which is the dinner-test payoff (a kid retells 'he was a PATENT CLERK'). ACCURACY RAIL: Einstein's Nobel was for the PHOTOELECTRIC paper, 1921, and relativity is not named in the citation -- never let a rung imply he won a prize for relativity. Second rail: the 1905 paper does NOT contain the string 'E=mc2'; he wrote m = L/V2 and the modern form came later -- and the paper is a question, not an announcement. Third rail: verify the Habicht-letter wording at build ('sehr revolutionaer' applied to the light-quantum paper only) and the 'salts of radium' closing line against the English translation before seeding either rung; drop the rung rather than paraphrase loosely. BANNED: any 'In what year did Einstein...' or 'Who discovered special relativity?' shell -- this is a wonder subject. Distractor mine: real adjacent 1900s physicists and real rival positions -- Lorentz, Poincare, Planck, Mach, Ostwald, Perrin, Minkowski -- and, for the Nobel rung, Einstein's own other three papers (all four choices stay live). Anti-restatement: never let a stem say 'atoms are real' before asking what the Brownian-motion paper showed. Lane border: this ladder owns the PAPERS and the physics; do not narrate Einstein's 1933 flight from Germany or his Roosevelt letter -- those are the history bank's.
history_overlap: HISTORY bank: Einstein as a 20th-century figure, his 1933 flight from Nazi Germany, and the 1939 Einstein-Szilard letter are plausibly history-bank facts. This ladder must key ONLY 1902-1905 Bern and the content of the four papers -- no exile, no bomb, no Roosevelt letter.

name: E=mc2: the smallest number with the biggest appetite
scope: A CONCEPT/THEME ladder: one equation displayed across the named cases where the mass actually went missing and someone weighed it. T1: the Sun fuses about 600 million tonnes of hydrogen every second -- but only about 4 million tonnes of that becomes energy; the knowable thing is WHY: a helium nucleus weighs about 0.7% less than the four hydrogen nuclei that made it, and that missing 0.7% is the sunlight. T2: Christmas 1938, Kungaelv in Sweden -- Lise Meitner, in exile from Berlin, walking in the snow with her nephew Otto Frisch after a letter from Otto Hahn reporting barium where barium had no business being; on a scrap of paper she weighed the fragments against the original nucleus, found the deficit, put it through E=mc2 and got about 200 million electron-volts per split. T3: Frisch needed a word for it and borrowed one from biology -- he asked about cell division and named it 'fission'; he then went to Copenhagen and measured the ~200 MeV directly, confirming his aunt's arithmetic. T4: nuclear versus chemical -- burning one carbon atom releases a few electron-volts; splitting one uranium nucleus releases about 200 million. The ratio (roughly a hundred million to one) is why a lump of uranium the size of a golf ball can do what a coal train does. T5: most of YOUR mass is not matter at all -- the three quarks inside a proton account for only about 1% of its 938 MeV; the other 99% is the energy of the strong-force field binding them, showing up as mass exactly as E=mc2 says it must. T5b: total conversion, in a hospital -- when an electron meets a positron, 100% of both masses becomes light: two photons of 511 keV flying back-to-back, which is precisely what a PET scanner is built to catch. T5c: the honest limit -- a charged phone battery really is heavier than a flat one, by about a picogram; the effect is real, universal, and far too small to weigh.
source: Grokipedia 'Mass-energy equivalence' (Einstein's 1905 derivation, m = L/V2, ~200 MeV per fission event, electron-positron annihilation at 1.022 MeV total, c2 ~ 9x10^16 J/kg); Grokipedia 'Lise Meitner' (Kungaelv Christmas 1938, the walk with Frisch, liquid-drop model, the back-of-envelope E=mc2 estimate of ~200 MeV, Frisch coining 'fission' from cell division, Frisch's ionization measurement at the Bohr Institute, Nature 11 Feb 1939, Hahn's sole 1944 Nobel, 'I will have nothing to do with a bomb!'); OpenStax/UCF Astronomy 16.2 and school-physics solar-energy references (~600 Mt/s hydrogen fused, ~4 Mt/s converted, the 0.71% helium mass deficit).
framing_note: CONCEPT/THEME ladder -- the analytic backbone of the sub-strand; every rung is a concrete named case, never the bare equation. INVERT THE WONDER throughout: the astonishing tonnage/voltage goes in the STEM, the knowable mechanism is the answer. Dinner-test payoff: T5 (99% of your weight is field energy, not stuff) and T2 (a Nobel-grade physics result worked out on a walk in the snow). ACCURACY RAIL: Meitner and Frisch did the PHYSICS; Hahn and Strassmann did the chemistry that found barium -- and the 1944 Nobel went to Hahn alone. Say the division of labour correctly and do not turn the Nobel snub into the rung's whole point here (that is a figure story, not this ladder's thread). Second rail: Grokipedia's '0.1 MeV for chemical bonds' is high -- chemical bond energies are a few eV; build the T4 comparison at a few eV vs 200 MeV and state the ratio as ~10^8. Distractor mine: real rival explanations for the Sun's power that serious people held -- gravitational contraction (Kelvin-Helmholtz), ordinary chemical burning, radioactive decay of internal radium -- plus real adjacent physicists (Hahn, Strassmann, Bohr, Chadwick, Fermi, Joliot-Curie). Never a joke option. Lane border: the Manhattan Project, Hiroshima, and Meitner's flight from Nazi Germany as narrative belong to HISTORY -- this ladder stops at the physics and the measurement.
history_overlap: HISTORY bank: the Manhattan Project and Hiroshima as WWII narrative; Meitner's 1938 escape from Nazi Germany and Hahn's conduct under the regime are plausible history-bank material. This ladder keys only the mass-deficit physics, the Kungaelv calculation, Frisch's naming and confirmation, and the modern cases (quark binding energy, PET annihilation). Build NO bomb-history rung.

name: Time really runs slower down here -- and your phone proves it
scope: A CONCEPT/THEME ladder on time dilation, deepened across the machines that had to be corrected for it. T1: every GPS satellite's clock runs about 38 microseconds a day fast relative to the ground; the hook is that 38 millionths of a second sounds like nothing -- the knowable payoff is that uncorrected it would push your map off by roughly 11 kilometres in a single day, because the receiver turns clock time into distance at the speed of light. T2: the correction is a fight between two effects pulling opposite ways -- the satellite is high up in weaker gravity, which makes its clock gain about +45.85 microseconds a day, and it is moving fast, which makes it lose about -7.2; gravity wins, and the net is about +38.6. T3: the engineers did not trust Einstein. NTS-2, launched 23 June 1977 with the first caesium clock ever put in orbit, carried a frequency synthesizer that could be switched ON or OFF -- they ran the clock uncorrected for about 20 days first to see whether the predicted shift was really there. It was: the measured rate came out +442.5 parts in 10^12, differing from the relativistic prediction by only 3.97 parts in 10^12. Then they flipped the switch. T4: Hafele and Keating, 1971 -- an $8,000 grant from the Office of Naval Research, of which $7,600 went on eight round-the-world plane tickets because the four caesium clocks needed their own seats. Flying east predicted -40 +/- 23 nanoseconds and gave -59 +/- 10; flying west predicted +275 +/- 21 and gave +273 +/- 7. The westbound clocks came home AHEAD of the ones left at the Naval Observatory. T5: the effect has been squeezed down to human scale -- Pound and Rebka in 1959 caught gravitational redshift over about 22 metres of a Harvard tower using iron-57 gamma rays and the Moessbauer effect; NIST in 2010 measured the difference between two aluminium-ion clocks 33 centimetres apart in height; a JILA/NIST strontium clock in 2022 resolved it across ONE MILLIMETRE inside a single cloud of atoms. T5b: the invitation -- your head has therefore aged very slightly more than your feet, by a few tens of nanoseconds over a lifetime, and the number is calculable from gh/c2.
source: Wikipedia 'Error analysis for the Global Positioning System' (+45,850 ns/day gravitational, -7,214 ns/day kinematic, net +38,640 ns/day; factory offset 10.22999999543 MHz; ~11.4 km/day positional drift if uncorrected); Neil Ashby, 'Relativity in the Global Positioning System', Living Reviews in Relativity 2003, and leapsecond.com's reprint of Ashby on NTS-2 (launch 23 June 1977, first orbiting caesium clock, the on/off synthesizer, ~20-day uncorrected run, +442.5 parts in 10^12 measured, 3.97 parts in 10^12 residual); Wikipedia 'Hafele-Keating experiment' ($8,000 ONR grant, $7,600 on eight tickets, HP 5061A clocks, eastward -40+/-23 predicted vs -59+/-10 observed, westward +275+/-21 vs +273+/-7, gravitational and kinematic components); Grokipedia 'Tests of general relativity' (Pound-Rebka 1959 Harvard tower with Fe-57 and the Moessbauer effect, refined to 1% in 1960; NIST 2010 aluminium-ion clocks at 33 cm; JILA/NIST 2022 strontium clocks across 1 mm; GPS relativistic corrections).
framing_note: CONCEPT/THEME ladder and the sub-strand's TEST-IT-YOURSELF centre of gravity -- the whole point is that this is not exotic, it is running in the kid's pocket right now. Dinner-test payoff: T3 (they built an OFF SWITCH for Einstein because they were not sure he was right) -- that rung is the flagship and must be the one a kid retells. INVERT THE WONDER on T1: 38 microseconds in the stem, the 11 km/day consequence as the answer. ACCURACY RAIL: the two effects have OPPOSITE signs and must never be collapsed -- +45.85 gravitational, -7.2 velocity, net +38.6 microseconds per day; a rung that says 'time dilation makes GPS clocks run slow' is wrong. Second rail: Pound-Rebka is 1959 (a 1960 run refined it) and the tower is about 22 m -- sources give 22.5 and 22.6 m, so write 'about 22 metres' rather than hinge a rung on the decimal. Third rail: state Hafele-Keating's error bars honestly -- the eastward result agreed within about 0.8 sigma, not perfectly; the westward result was the clean one. Distractor mine: real rival explanations engineers actually had to rule out -- clock drift/ageing, temperature and magnetic-field effects on caesium standards, orbital-model error, ionospheric delay -- plus the real adjacent effects (Sagnac, Doppler, Shapiro delay). Anti-restatement: never let the stem say 'gravity makes high clocks run fast' before asking which effect wins. Lane border: GPS as a MAPPING technology is geography's; this ladder owns the CLOCK.
history_overlap: GEOGRAPHY bank: satellite navigation / GPS as a map-making and wayfinding technology is plausibly a geography topic. This ladder must key only the clock physics (the two-sign correction, NTS-2's switch, Hafele-Keating, Pound-Rebka, the millimetre-scale clocks) and never tour how maps are made.

name: The muons that should never have reached the ground
scope: The everyday particle proof of time dilation, and the one relativity experiment a determined kid can actually run. T1: a muon is created about 15 kilometres up when a cosmic ray smashes into the top of the atmosphere, and it lives on average 2.2 microseconds; even at 99.5% of the speed of light that is only about 660 metres of travel. The knowable payoff: they arrive anyway -- roughly one muon per square centimetre per minute is passing through your hand right now. T2: David Frisch and James Smith, 1963, counted them. On Mount Washington in New Hampshire (1,917 m) they logged about 563 muons an hour. Ordinary physics said about 27 an hour should survive the trip to sea level in Cambridge, Massachusetts. They counted about 412. T3: it had been done before, and earlier -- Bruno Rossi and D. B. Hall in 1940 compared muon counts at Echo Lake, Colorado (3,240 m) against Denver (1,616 m) and found the fast ones outliving the slow ones, more than twenty years before the famous version. T4: the mind-bender is that from the MUON's point of view nothing slows down at all -- its own 2.2 microseconds tick by normally; what changes is that the 15 kilometres of atmosphere is squashed to a few hundred metres. Time dilation and length contraction are the same fact seen from two seats. T5: the sharpest version is a storage ring -- in the muon g-2 experiments at CERN and Fermilab muons circulate at a gamma factor of about 29, and they survive about 29 times their rest lifetime, matching the relativistic prediction to a fraction of a percent. T5b: the invitation -- a dry-ice cloud chamber in a shoebox shows the muon tracks as white threads, and MIT's open-source CosmicWatch desktop detector (a scintillator, a silicon photomultiplier and a microcontroller) can be built for under $100 in about four hours; count muons at sea level, then count them again at the top of a mountain.
source: Wikipedia 'Experimental testing of time dilation' (Rossi-Hall 1940 at Echo Lake 3,240 m and Denver 1,616 m, mean proper lifetime ~2.2 us; Frisch-Smith 1963 Mount Washington 1,917 m to Cambridge sea level, ~563/hr summit, ~27/hr classically predicted, ~412/hr observed, velocities 0.995-0.9954c, measured dilation factor 8.8 +/- 0.8); Axani et al., 'The CosmicWatch Desktop Muon Detector', JINST 13 (2018) P03019 and arXiv:1801.03029 / arXiv:2508.12111 (under $100 in parts, ~4 hours to build, scintillator + SiPM, open-source Arduino/Python).
framing_note: DISCOVERY/EXPERIMENT ladder, and the clearest TEST-IT-YOURSELF payoff in the sub-strand. Dinner-test payoff: T2 -- '27 should have made it, 412 did' is the number a kid repeats. INVERT THE WONDER on T1: the 660-metre range goes in the stem as the impossibility, and the survival is the answer. ACCURACY RAIL: 2.2 microseconds is the muon's MEAN lifetime in its own rest frame, not a fixed expiry -- decay is probabilistic, and the comparison Frisch and Smith made was between two counting rates, not between individual particles; write it that way. Second rail: verify the sea-level flux figure (~1 muon per cm2 per minute) at build against a current particle-data reference before seeding the T1 payoff. Teach-before-test: 'muon' and 'mean lifetime' must be introduced in an earlier rung's stem before any rung leans on them. Distractor mine: the real physics that had to be excluded -- muons being produced lower down, misidentified electrons or protons, detector dead-time, atmospheric absorption slowing them -- plus the genuinely competing relativistic account (length contraction) used honestly as the OTHER true description, which the T4 rung then resolves rather than as a wrong option. Never a joke option. Lane border: cosmic rays as an astronomy/particle topic and cloud chambers as a detector story may sit in another physics sub-strand -- this ladder is anchored on the TIME-DILATION test and must key the counting experiments.

name: Eddington's eclipse: the test that made Einstein famous overnight
scope: 29 May 1919, and how a measurement gets judged. T1: the scene -- a British Quaker astronomer, a conscientious objector who had nearly been imprisoned during the war and was released on condition he lead this expedition, waited out a rainy morning on Principe, a small island in the Gulf of Guinea, and got a gap in the clouds during totality; the answer is Arthur Eddington, sent to test a GERMAN's theory months after the armistice. T2: there were THREE numbers on the table, not two -- zero if light is a pure wave untouched by gravity, 0.87 arcseconds if light is a stream of corpuscles falling under Newtonian gravity (Soldner had computed this in 1801), and 1.75 arcseconds from general relativity; the knowable point is that Einstein's 1915 value was exactly DOUBLE his own earlier 1911 prediction. T3: the near-miss that saved him -- Erwin Finlay-Freundlich took a German team to Crimea for the August 1914 eclipse to make this very measurement, and when war broke out he was interned in Russia and the expedition failed. At that moment Einstein's published prediction was still the WRONG 0.87. T4: what actually came back. At Sobral in Brazil the big 13-inch astrograph was ruined -- heat distorted the coelostat mirror -- and its plates were set aside; the trustworthy number came from a 4-inch backup lens, 1.98 arcseconds. Eddington's cloud-broken Principe plates gave 1.61. Both sit near 1.75 and far from 0.87. T5: the accusation and the audit -- in 1980 John Earman and Clark Glymour argued that Eddington discarded the Sobral 13-inch data because it favoured Newton, i.e. that he found what he wanted; re-measurement of the surviving original plates at Greenwich in 1979 and Daniel Kennefick's re-analysis found the exclusion was justified by a real, quantifiable systematic error, and the result stands. T5b: the aftermath -- at the joint Royal Society / Royal Astronomical Society meeting of 6 November 1919 the Society's president J. J. Thomson called it 'the most important result obtained in connection with the theory of gravitation since Newton's day'; the next morning The Times of London ran 'Revolution in Science / New Theory of the Universe / Newtonian Ideas Overthrown', and an obscure Berlin professor became the most famous scientist alive.
source: Grokipedia 'Eddington experiment' (Principe and Sobral, Eddington + Cottingham and Crommelin + Davidson, Principe 1.61 and Sobral 4-inch 1.98, the 13-inch coelostat distortion, the three competing predictions including Soldner's 1801 0.87 arcsec, Eddington's conscientious-objector exemption, Dyson's 1917 proposal, the 6 Nov 1919 joint meeting, Earman-Glymour 1980 and the modern re-examinations); Grokipedia 'Tests of general relativity' (1.75 arcsec GR prediction, 1919 values, later VLBI confirmation to 0.03%); Wikipedia 'Erwin Finlay-Freundlich' (1914 eclipse expedition, internment in Russia, prisoner exchange, expedition failed); Royal Society Notes and Records 76(1) 2022, 'The 1919 eclipse results that verified general relativity and their later detractors' and arXiv:1409.7812 (the data-selection debate and the 1979 Greenwich re-measurement); Smithsonian Magazine and earthsky.org for the J. J. Thomson quotation and The Times headline of 7 November 1919.
framing_note: DISCOVERY + REVERSAL, and the sub-strand's keystone 'what does a good test look like' ladder. Dinner-test payoff: T3 -- the war wrecked the 1914 expedition that would have measured Einstein against his own wrong number. ACCURACY RAIL (the load-bearing one): the 1919 result was GOOD but not decisive on its own -- the error bars were large, published probable errors differ from modern standard errors (1.98 is quoted with +/-0.12 and with +/-0.18; 1.61 with +/-0.30 and with +/-0.45), so never build a rung whose answer hinges on an error bar, and never say the eclipse 'proved' relativity. Say what is true: it excluded the Newtonian half-value, and later radio interferometry confirmed the deflection to 0.03%. Second rail: Eddington's 1919 measurement is DEFLECTION OF STARLIGHT, not gravitational lensing images -- keep them separate. Third rail: 0.87 arcseconds is BOTH the Newtonian-corpuscle value (Soldner 1801) and Einstein's own 1911 error; say so, because the doubling is the whole drama. Distractor mine: the real live alternatives -- no deflection at all, the Newtonian 0.87, atmospheric refraction, plate-scale change from temperature, and real adjacent astronomers (Dyson, Crommelin, Davidson, Campbell at Lick). Anti-restatement: describe what the plates SHOWED (stars displaced outward from the Sun) and let the competing predicted values be recalled, never stated in the stem. Lane border: WWI and Anglo-German post-war feeling belong to HISTORY; and the T5 rung must stay a WORKING-PRACTICE question -- when is discarding data legitimate? -- not a Kuhn/theory-ladenness seminar, which is philosophy's.
history_overlap: HISTORY bank: World War I, the armistice, and post-war anti-German feeling in British institutions are history-bank territory -- this ladder keys the expedition, the instruments and the plates, not the war. PHILOSOPHY bank: theory-laden observation and confirmation bias as epistemology are philosophy's; the T5 rung must be framed as practice (was there a real systematic error?), and its resolution -- the 1979 re-measurement -- must be the answer.

name: Mercury's stubborn 43 arcseconds and the planet that wasn't there
scope: The anomaly that killed a planet and crowned a theory. T1: Mercury's orbit does not close -- the point of closest approach creeps forward, and after Newton's gravity plus the pull of every known planet is subtracted there are about 43 arcseconds per century left over that nothing accounts for. Urbain Le Verrier, who in 1846 had famously found Neptune by exactly this method (an unexplained wobble means an unseen body), announced in 1859 that the leftover meant another planet, inside Mercury's orbit, and named it Vulcan. T2: in December 1859 Le Verrier received a letter from Edmond Lescarbault, a country doctor and amateur astronomer at Orgeres-en-Beauce, claiming he had watched a small dark dot cross the face of the Sun that March. Le Verrier took a train, arrived unannounced, interrogated him -- and believed him. Lescarbault was made a Chevalier of the Legion d'honneur for observing a planet that does not exist. T3: Vulcan was hunted for more than fifty years and repeatedly 'seen'; eclipse expeditions (including the celebrated 1878 claims of James Craig Watson and Lewis Swift) reported it and could never be confirmed by anyone else. T4: in November 1915, days after finishing his field equations, Einstein fed Mercury's orbit into them -- and 43 arcseconds per century fell out with nothing adjusted to make it fit. He wrote to Paul Ehrenfest that he had been 'beside myself with joyous excitement' and told Adriaan Fokker the result gave him heart palpitations. T5: how you even SEE 43 arcseconds a century -- the raw observed precession relative to Earth's equinox is about 5,600 arcseconds per century, of which roughly 5,025 is our own coordinate system moving (the precession of the equinoxes) and about 532 is the other planets; the anomaly exists only after you subtract, very carefully, everything you already know. T5b: the modern verdict -- radar echoes bounced off Mercury from 1966 to 1990 pinned the relativistic precession to within 0.1%, and the MESSENGER orbiter (2011-2015) tightened it further. T5c: the method lesson -- Le Verrier's identical move gave Neptune (a new object) and Vulcan (nothing); the same anomaly can mean a missing body or a broken law, and only the test tells you which.
source: Grokipedia 'Tests of general relativity' (574 arcsec/century total relative to the fixed stars, 531-532 from Newtonian planetary perturbations, ~43 residual; Le Verrier 1859 analysis of 1697-1848 transits giving ~38 and the Vulcan hypothesis; Newcomb 1882 refining to ~43; Einstein's November 1915 Schwarzschild-metric derivation giving 42.98; radar ranging 1966-1990 to 0.1%; MESSENGER 2011-2015); Wikipedia 'Edmond Modeste Lescarbault' and 'Vulcan (hypothetical planet)' (the 26 March 1859 claimed transit, Le Verrier's unannounced visit to Orgeres-en-Beauce, the Legion d'honneur, later Watson and Swift claims); Janssen & Renn, 'Einstein and the Perihelion Motion of Mercury' (Max Planck Institute) and the Einstein-Besso manuscript literature (18 November 1915 submission; the letters to Ehrenfest and Fokker).
framing_note: REVERSAL + DISCOVERY. Dinner-test payoff: T2 -- a country doctor got a knighthood for spotting a planet that was never there. Voice: the drama is that Le Verrier's method was not stupid, it was PROVEN (it had just produced Neptune), which is exactly why the failure matters. ACCURACY RAIL (do not muddle this): the leftover is ~43 arcseconds per century, but the total number quoted depends on the reference frame -- ~574/century measured against the fixed stars, ~5,600/century measured against Earth's moving equinox. Pick ONE frame per rung and say which; never put 574 and 5,600 in the same rung as if they described the same thing. Second rail: Einstein's reaction is documented in his own letters (Ehrenfest: 'beside myself with joyous excitement'; palpitations reported to Fokker) -- if a rung uses a quotation it must be one of those, verified against the Collected Papers at build, or use no quotation at all. Third rail: relativity did not 'fit' the 43 -- it had no free parameter to fit with, which is the point of the T4 rung. Distractor mine: the real live explanations serious astronomers held -- an unseen inner planet (Vulcan), a ring of asteroids inside Mercury's orbit, solar oblateness, a modified inverse-square exponent (Asaph Hall's proposal), and a dragging effect from the solar corona. Anti-restatement: never say 'Einstein's theory explained it' in a stem that asks what explained it. Lane border: Neptune's discovery as an astronomy story may belong to another sub-strand -- here Neptune appears only as the precedent that made Vulcan credible.

name: Gravity is not a pull: the falling man, the sealed elevator, and what the rubber sheet gets wrong
scope: The CONCEPT ladder that carries the sub-strand's analytic ceiling. T1: sitting in his chair at the Bern patent office in 1907, Einstein pictured a man falling off a roof -- and realised the man would not feel his own weight at all. He later called it the happiest thought of his life; the payoff is that free fall feels like NOTHING, which is why astronauts float. T2: the sealed elevator. In a windowless box you cannot tell whether you are standing on Earth or being accelerated at 1g through empty space -- and Einstein pulled a testable consequence straight out of that in 1911: a light beam crossing the box must appear to bend. T3: the second consequence from the same box -- a clock at the ceiling and a clock at the floor cannot agree; gravity changes the rate at which time passes, predicted 1911 and caught in a Harvard tower by Pound and Rebka in 1959. T4: the rubber sheet is a LIE that helps. It explains gravity by using gravity (the bowling ball only sinks because real gravity pulls it down), it shows a two-dimensional slice of a four-dimensional thing, and worst of all it shows curved SPACE -- whereas for anything moving slowly, like a thrown ball or a falling apple, almost all of the effect comes from the curvature of TIME. T5: nothing is pulling on a falling object. An object in free fall feels no force whatever and travels the straightest available path through curved spacetime; the thing that actually feels a force is you, standing still, being shoved upward by the floor. Astronauts on the ISS are not beyond gravity -- gravity up there is about 90% of its strength at the ground -- they are simply falling, and missing. T5b: how hard the equivalence has been tested -- Lorand Eoetvoes's torsion balance reached about one part in a billion by 1908, and the MICROSCOPE satellite pushed it to one part in 10^15 in 2022; on 2 August 1971 David Scott dropped a hammer and a falcon feather on the Moon in front of a camera and they hit the dust together. T5c: John Wheeler's one-line summary of the whole theory -- spacetime tells matter how to move, matter tells spacetime how to curve.
source: Wikipedia 'Equivalence principle' (Einstein's 1907 Bern insight and his 1922 Kyoto recollection 'if a man falls freely, he would not feel his weight'; the elevator; the 1911 predictions of light bending and clock-rate differences; Eoetvoes 1908 to ~1 in 10^9; MICROSCOPE 2022 to 10^-15); Grokipedia 'Tests of general relativity' (Pound-Rebka 1959 and its 1960 refinement; the 1911 equivalence-principle deflection value versus the 1915 full-curvature value); Grokipedia 'Eddington experiment' (Einstein's 1911 0.875 arcsec from the equivalence principle alone, doubled once spatial curvature is included); Science & Education 27 (2018) 593, 'Understanding Curved Spacetime: the Role of the Rubber Sheet Analogy in Learning General Relativity', and the OAPT article 'General Relativity: Beyond the Bowling Ball and the Trampoline' (the analogy's documented failure modes, including that it models Newtonian gravity and hides the dominance of time curvature); J. A. Wheeler, Geons, Black Holes and Quantum Foam (1998) for the summary line; NASA Apollo 15 mission record for the 2 August 1971 hammer-and-feather demonstration.
framing_note: CONCEPT/THEME ladder with two CORRECTED-MISCONCEPTION rungs, which are on-voice gold: the rubber sheet (T4) and 'astronauts float because there is no gravity' (T5). Dinner-test payoff: T5 -- the falling person feels no force and YOU are the one being pushed. ACCURACY RAIL: do not overclaim the rubber sheet's failure -- the honest statement is that it is a useful picture whose limits are specific and nameable (it presupposes gravity, it is a 2-D slice, and it depicts spatial curvature when time curvature dominates for slow motion); never let a rung say 'spacetime is not curved' or 'the analogy is worthless'. Second rail: the 'happiest thought' phrasing comes from Einstein's own later recollections (the 1920 unpublished Nature manuscript and the 1922 Kyoto address), not from a 1907 notebook -- attribute it as his own retelling, the same way the bank handles Newton's apple. Third rail: ISS gravity is roughly 90% of surface strength at ~400 km -- give the number, do not say 'almost none'. Teach-before-test: 'geodesic' and 'equivalence principle' must be taught in an earlier stem before any rung leans on them. Distractor mine: the real wrong pictures people hold and the real rivals -- gravity as an instantaneous Newtonian force, gravity as a pulling 'field' of the electromagnetic kind, Le Sage's push gravity, Mach's principle, and the genuine but incomplete 1911 equivalence-principle-only prediction. Lane border: thought experiments as a REASONING GENRE belong to philosophy; here the elevator is a physicist's instrument that produced two numbers somebody later measured.
history_overlap: PHILOSOPHY bank: thought experiments as a method, and 'what makes an analogy break down', are philosophy-bank reasoning moves. This ladder must keep the elevator and the rubber sheet tied to specific measured consequences (1911 light bending, 1911 clock rates, Pound-Rebka, Eoetvoes, MICROSCOPE, Apollo 15) rather than discussing analogy as such.

name: Gravitational waves: predicted 1916, doubted by Einstein, heard in 2015
scope: A century between the prediction and the sound. T1: on 14 September 2015 at 09:50:45 UTC, LIGO's two detectors were not even officially observing yet -- the upgraded machines were still in engineering mode, four days before the science run was due to start -- when a signal swept through in about a fifth of a second, rising from 35 to 250 hertz in roughly eight cycles. It was two black holes of about 36 and 29 solar masses merging about 1.3 billion light-years away. T2: the size of what they measured. The wave changed the length of a 4-kilometre arm by roughly a thousandth of the width of a proton, and the machine could tell. T3: how they knew it came from the sky and not from a passing truck -- the same wave peaks arrived at Livingston, Louisiana about 7 milliseconds BEFORE they arrived at Hanford, Washington, which is what a ripple crossing 3,000 km at light speed does. T4: Einstein himself decided they did not exist. In 1936 he and Nathan Rosen sent Physical Review a paper titled 'Do Gravitational Waves Exist?' arguing that they do not; the anonymous referee -- Howard Percy Robertson -- found the error, Einstein wrote an indignant letter to editor John Tate saying he saw no reason to address the 'in any case erroneous' opinion of the referee, withdrew the paper and vowed never to publish there again. Then he quietly accepted the correction and published the opposite conclusion in the Journal of the Franklin Institute in 1937. T5: the argument that settled whether the waves carry real energy came from Richard Feynman at the 1957 Chapel Hill conference -- two beads on a stiff rod with a little friction; a passing wave slides them, friction makes heat, therefore the wave did work. Hermann Bondi wrote it up. T5b: we had already heard them indirectly. Russell Hulse and Joseph Taylor's binary pulsar PSR B1913+16, found in 1974, is losing orbital energy and its 7.75-hour orbit is shrinking at exactly the rate the quadrupole formula predicts, to within 0.2% -- the 1993 Nobel. T5c: for a few milliseconds GW150914 radiated about 3.6 x 10^49 watts -- more power than all the light of every star in the observable universe combined -- and not one photon of it was light. T5d: on 17 August 2017 a neutron-star merger arrived as both a gravitational wave and, 1.7 seconds later, a gamma-ray burst, pinning the speed of gravity to the speed of light to about one part in 10^15.
source: Grokipedia 'First observation of gravitational waves' (GW150914 on 14 Sept 2015 at 09:50:45 UTC, 36 and 29 solar masses, ~62 final, ~3 solar masses radiated, 410 Mpc / ~1.3 billion ly, strain ~10^-21, SNR 24, announced 11 Feb 2016, 2017 Nobel to Weiss, Barish and Thorne; Einstein's 1916 prediction and his 1918 correction; Weber's resonant bars; Hulse-Taylor PSR B1913+16 discovered 1974, 7.75-hour orbit, Pdot = -2.423e-12 s/s matching GR to 0.2%, 1993 Nobel; PSR J0737-3039A/B to better than 0.1%; GW170817 constraining wave speed to <10^-15 of c); Wikipedia 'GW150914' (0.2 s signal, 35-250 Hz in about 8 cycles, 7 ms Livingston-before-Hanford, peak emission 3.6 x 10^49 W exceeding all starlight in the observable universe, detection during engineering mode days before the 18 Sept science run, length change ~1/1000 of a proton width); Wikipedia 'Sticky bead argument' (Feynman at the 1957 Chapel Hill conference, Bondi's write-up; the 1936 Einstein-Rosen submission to Physical Review, referee H. P. Robertson, Einstein's letter to editor John Tate, republication as 'On Gravitational Waves', Journal of the Franklin Institute, 1937).
framing_note: DISCOVERY ladder with a REVERSAL at its heart. Dinner-test payoff: T4 -- EINSTEIN was the one who said gravitational waves do not exist, and an anonymous referee was right. That rung is why this ladder earns deep. Voice: present it straight -- the referee found a real mathematical error, Einstein was angry, and Einstein changed his mind; no gloating in either direction, and no lesson-stapling about peer review in general. ACCURACY RAIL: LIGO measures a length CHANGE, not a length -- write the strain as a fractional change over the 4 km arm (about a thousandth of a proton's width; Wikipedia expresses it over the 1,120 km effective folded path, so state whichever you use and do not mix them). Second rail: the 1993 Nobel was for the INDIRECT evidence (orbital decay), the 2017 Nobel for the direct detection -- never let a rung imply Hulse and Taylor detected a wave. Third rail: Joseph Weber's 1969 bar-detector claims were never replicated -- if a rung uses Weber, say that honestly; he built the field and his specific detections did not hold up. Distractor mine: the real rival explanations LIGO had to exclude -- seismic noise, thermal noise, a truck, a lightning strike, a deliberate blind injection (the collaboration really did run those) -- plus real adjacent physicists (Weber, Wheeler, Bondi, Thorne, Weiss, Drever). Anti-restatement: T3's stem gives the 7 ms fact and asks what it established; never state 'it came from space' first. Lane border: the forging of gold and platinum in the GW170817 kilonova is an astronomy/chemistry wonder -- mention the event, do not build the nucleosynthesis rung here.
history_overlap: PHILOSOPHY bank: peer review and falsification as epistemology belong there. The 1936 Robertson rung must stay concrete working practice -- a referee caught a specific mathematical error in a specific paper and the author was wrong -- not a general argument about whether peer review works. ASTRONOMY/other physics sub-strand: heavy-element formation in the GW170817 kilonova should be built there, not here.

name: The ether that was not there
scope: The most famous failed experiment in physics, and the theory it killed. T1: Cleveland, July 1887. Albert Michelson and Edward Morley floated a heavy sandstone slab on a pool of liquid mercury so their apparatus could be rotated without a shudder, split a beam of light down two perpendicular arms and looked for the interference fringes to shift as the Earth ploughed at 30 km/s through the ether. They expected a shift of about 0.4 of a fringe; they measured less than 0.02 -- nothing. T2: why every serious physicist believed in the ether anyway -- waves need something to wave in, as sound needs air, so light needed a medium; the trouble was that to carry light at 300,000 km/s it had to be stiffer than steel, while being so insubstantial the planets sailed through it without slowing. Physicists knew this was absurd and kept it anyway, because nothing better was on offer. T3: the rescue. George FitzGerald in 1889 and Hendrik Lorentz in 1892 proposed that moving objects physically CONTRACT along their direction of motion, by precisely the amount needed to hide the ether wind -- the right formula reached by a wrong route, invented to save a doomed hypothesis. T4: the anomaly was not brushed aside. Dayton Miller, working from Mount Wilson through the 1920s and 1930s, reported a small but persistent ether drift and was taken seriously for decades; only Robert Shankland's 1955 re-analysis traced Miller's signal to temperature gradients in his hut. T5: the corrected misconception. The textbook chain 'Michelson-Morley proved the ether does not exist, so Einstein invented relativity' is tidier than the record: Einstein's 1905 paper never names the experiment, referring only to 'unsuccessful attempts to discover any motion of the earth relatively to the light medium', and historians still argue over how much it actually influenced him -- his own stated starting point was an asymmetry in how Maxwell's equations described a magnet and a coil.
source: Grokipedia 'Michelson-Morley experiment' (1887 at the Case School of Applied Science, Cleveland; mercury float and sandstone slab; ~11 m effective arm length; predicted ~0.40 fringe shift versus observed <0.02; observations 8-12 July 1887; Michelson's 1881 solo attempt; Fresnel drag and Fizeau 1851; Airy 1871; Dayton Miller's 1920s ether-drift claims; the ether's required stiffness and the 30 km/s orbital speed); Wikipedia 'Michelson-Morley experiment' and 'Luminiferous aether' for the FitzGerald 1889 / Lorentz 1892 contraction and Shankland's 1955 analysis of Miller; Einstein, 'Zur Elektrodynamik bewegter Koerper' (1905), opening paragraph, for the magnet-and-conductor asymmetry and the unnamed 'unsuccessful attempts'.
framing_note: REVERSAL ladder; the ether is the richest single distractor in the whole bank and this ladder earns the right to use it honestly everywhere else. Dinner-test payoff: T1 -- they floated the whole experiment on a pond of mercury so it could be turned smoothly. ACCURACY RAIL: do NOT tell the tidy textbook chain. The honest statement for T5 is that the 1905 paper does not name Michelson and Morley, that Einstein cited the magnet-and-conductor asymmetry as his own motivation, and that historians genuinely disagree about the experiment's influence on him -- write the disagreement as a disagreement. Second rail: the Lorentz-FitzGerald contraction is not 'wrong' as an equation; it is the same length contraction relativity later derived, arrived at as an ad hoc rescue -- say that precisely, because a sloppy rung here teaches a falsehood. Third rail: Michelson himself never embraced relativity and went on hunting the ether; Dayton Miller's positive results were investigated for thirty years, not suppressed -- this is the bank's honest picture of how anomalies are actually handled. Distractor mine: the ether itself in all its forms (stationary ether, fully dragged ether, Fresnel's partial drag), plus the real adjacent experiments (Fizeau's flowing water 1851, Airy's water-filled telescope 1871, Kennedy-Thorndike, Ives-Stilwell). Anti-restatement: T1's stem must give the expected shift and let 'nothing' be the recalled result, never announce the null result first. Lane border: interferometry as an OPTICAL instrument and the wave nature of light belong to a light/optics sub-strand -- this ladder keys the death of the ether and the setup for 1905.

name: Black holes: from a trench on the Russian front to a photograph
scope: Relativity's most extreme prediction, and the fifty years nobody believed it. T1: Einstein published his field equations in November 1915 expecting that exact solutions would take years. Within weeks a letter arrived from the Russian front: Karl Schwarzschild, a German astronomer serving as an artillery lieutenant computing shell trajectories, had solved them exactly, and dated the letter 22 December 1915. Einstein wrote back that he had not expected the exact solution could be formulated so simply. Schwarzschild contracted pemphigus, an autoimmune skin disease, at the front and died on 11 May 1916, aged 42. T2: for decades the solution's central point was treated as a mathematical embarrassment rather than a place -- and the phrase 'black hole' is not Einstein's or Schwarzschild's; John Archibald Wheeler made it stick from 1967, after it had already appeared in print a few years earlier. T3: the ugliest moment. Subrahmanyan Chandrasekhar worked out on the boat to England in 1930 that a white dwarf above about 1.44 solar masses cannot hold itself up; on 11 January 1935, at the Royal Astronomical Society, Arthur Eddington -- the hero of the 1919 eclipse, at the height of his authority -- rose after him and called it stellar buffoonery, in front of everyone. Chandrasekhar was right; the Nobel came in 1983, forty-eight years later. T4: Roger Penrose proved in 1965 that collapse to a singularity is not an artefact of assuming perfect symmetry but a robust consequence of general relativity -- the 2020 Nobel, shared with Reinhard Genzel and Andrea Ghez, who spent decades watching individual stars whip around an invisible mass at the centre of our galaxy. T5: on 10 April 2019 the Event Horizon Telescope released the shadow of M87*, and on 12 May 2022 the one at the centre of the Milky Way. It is not a photograph in the ordinary sense: eight radio observatories on four continents recorded raw data onto hard drives that were physically flown to central labs, and the image is a reconstruction from the interference between them.
source: Wikipedia 'Karl Schwarzschild' (Russian front, artillery lieutenant computing ballistics, letter to Einstein dated 22 December 1915, Einstein's reply 'I had not expected that one could formulate the exact solution of the problem in such a simple way', pemphigus, died 11 May 1916); MacTutor 'Chandrasekhar-Eddington' and IOPSpark 'Chandrasekhar's stellar buffoonery' (the 1.44 solar-mass limit, the RAS meeting of 11 January 1935, Eddington's undisclosed intention to speak against him, 'stellar buffoonery', the 1983 Nobel); NobelPrize.org, 'The Nobel Prize in Physics 2020' (Penrose 'for the discovery that black hole formation is a robust prediction of the general theory of relativity'; Genzel and Ghez for the supermassive compact object at the galactic centre); Event Horizon Telescope collaboration releases and NASA/JPL 'How Scientists Captured the First Image of a Black Hole' (M87* April 2019, Sagittarius A* 12 May 2022, VLBI across continents, data shipped on physical drives).
framing_note: DISCOVERY + REVERSAL. Dinner-test payoff: T1 -- he solved Einstein's equations in a war trench and was dead within five months. Second payoff: T3, because the hero of the 1919 eclipse ladder is the villain of this one, and the bank should let that stand without editorialising. ACCURACY RAIL: Wheeler POPULARIZED 'black hole' from 1967; he did not coin it (it appears in a 1964 report of an AAAS meeting) -- say 'made it stick', never 'named it'. Second rail: the EHT images show the SHADOW cast on surrounding hot glowing gas, not the hole itself and not an optical photograph; a rung that says 'they photographed a black hole' teaches a falsehood, and the reconstruction detail is the more interesting fact anyway. Third rail: Eddington's objection was not stupid -- he believed some unknown physics would prevent unlimited collapse; steel-man him before the vindication, per the bank's even-handed rails. Distractor mine: the real rival ideas -- that the Schwarzschild radius was a coordinate artefact with no physical meaning (which for a while it partly was), that degeneracy pressure always halts collapse, that the galactic-centre mass was a dense star cluster rather than a single object -- plus real adjacent figures (Oppenheimer and Snyder, Wheeler, Zwicky, Landau, Fowler). Lane border: this ladder is the RELATIVITY-PREDICTION story; if the bank has an astronomy or cosmology sub-strand, quasars, accretion discs, Hawking radiation and galaxy-formation belong there -- flag before build so the two do not duplicate M87*.
history_overlap: Intra-bank: an astronomy/cosmology sub-strand may also want the EHT images, Hawking radiation and the galactic centre. This ladder keys the prediction's chain of custody -- Schwarzschild's solution, the fifty years of disbelief, Chandrasekhar's humiliation, Penrose's theorem, the reconstruction of the shadow -- and must not tour black-hole astrophysics.

name: Einstein's lens: the effect he said we would never see
scope: A three-rung gem on gravitational lensing, keyed to the prediction and its overturning. T1: in 1936 Einstein published a short paper in Science, written only because an amateur, the Czech engineer Rudi Mandl, kept pestering him about it: a star lying behind another star would have its light bent around into a ring or a double image. In print and in his letters Einstein dismissed the idea as of no practical value, since the alignment required would essentially never occur -- he thought nobody would ever see it. T2: Fritz Zwicky spotted the fix within a year. In 1937 he pointed out that entire GALAXIES, being vastly more massive and vastly bigger targets, would lens far more often and far more strongly than single stars -- and that the effect would let astronomers weigh a galaxy directly from how hard it bends light past it. T3: it took until 1979. Dennis Walsh, Bob Carswell and Ray Weymann, using the 2.1-metre telescope at Kitt Peak, found two quasars sitting suspiciously close together with identical spectra -- not twins, but one quasar seen twice, its light split around an intervening galaxy. The 'Twin Quasar' Q0957+561 was the first gravitational lens ever confirmed, and today the same trick maps where dark matter sits by mapping where light bends with no visible mass to bend it.
source: Wikipedia 'Gravitational lens' (Einstein's 1912 notebook speculation; the 1936 Science paper 'Lens-Like Action of a Star by the Deviation of Light in the Gravitational Field' published at Rudi Mandl's urging, and Einstein's pessimism about ever observing it; Zwicky's 1937 proposal that galaxies would be far better lenses and could be weighed by lensing; Walsh, Carswell and Weymann's 1979 discovery of the Twin Quasar Q0957+561 with the Kitt Peak 2.1 m telescope; later Einstein rings and the use of lensing to map dark matter).
framing_note: MINI, three gems, one wonder each. The controlling voice is the REVERSAL against Einstein himself, which is why it is worth building even small: the man who predicted the effect declared it unobservable, and an amateur pest and an abrasive outsider between them turned it into a working instrument. Dinner-test payoff: T1 -- Einstein said we would never see it. ACCURACY RAIL: Einstein's dismissal must be attributed accurately -- he did NOT say lensing was impossible, he said the stellar alignment needed made observation hopeless; Zwicky's contribution was the change of target from stars to galaxies, not the discovery of lensing. Do not overstate Mandl's role either: he prompted the paper, he did not do the physics. Second rail: keep this distinct from the 1919 eclipse ladder -- that is deflection of starlight measured as a tiny angular shift; this is a source seen MULTIPLY. Distractor mine: real adjacent phenomena that could explain two nearby identical spectra -- a genuine physical pair of quasars, a foreground star's reflection, an instrumental ghost image -- plus real adjacent astronomers (Zwicky, Refsdal, Chwolson). Lane border: dark matter itself is a cosmology topic; here lensing appears only as the measuring tool, and the MYSTERY status of dark matter must be flagged rather than explained.
history_overlap: Intra-bank: dark matter as an open MYSTERY belongs to a cosmology/astronomy sub-strand -- this mini may reference lensing as the weighing method but must not build a dark-matter rung.
